title: Deformation Background
notes: Open the appendix as a compression move. The preceding chapter studied complex-structure deformations through the Maurer-Cartan equation; this appendix asks which algebraic ingredients made that argument work. The lecture should make dGBV algebras feel like a portable machine: product, differential, Delta operator, bracket, and a master equation.

title: What The Appendix Packages
notes: Use the roadmap to keep the abstractions from floating away. First the lecture builds the abstract dGBV language, then it identifies the same pattern inside polyvector-valued forms, and finally it explains why the Calabi-Yau volume form supplies the missing Delta operator. The final third is about formal solutions and the two hypotheses that make recursion possible.

title: Supercommutative Differential Algebra
notes: Start at the smallest algebraic level: the appendix only needs a parity grading, not a full integer grading. Every sign comes from moving odd objects past each other. The differential is odd, squares to zero, and obeys the graded Leibniz rule, so students should hear this as the algebraic shadow of the Dolbeault differential.

title: BV, GBV, And dGBV Operators
notes: Emphasize that Delta is not introduced as another derivation. It is an odd linear operator whose second-order failure produces derivations theta_a. If Delta also squares to zero, the structure is GBV; if an existing differential d anticommutes with Delta, the resulting package is dGBV. That compatibility is what later survives deformation.

title: The Derived Odd Bracket
notes: The bracket is not an extra primitive in the abstract definition; it is derived from the BV operator. The displayed identities say it behaves like a Lie bracket after shifting parity by one. The important teaching point is that d differentiates the bracket, so the bracket can measure whether a perturbed differential still squares to zero.

title: Deforming The Differential
notes: This is the first payoff slide. An even element phi produces a new odd derivation d_phi by adding the inner operation theta_phi. Squaring d_phi gives exactly the same shape as the deformation equation from complex structures: a linear term plus a quadratic bracket term. The master equation is therefore an obstruction-cancellation equation.

title: The Algebra Of Polyvector-Valued Forms
notes: Now move from abstract algebra back to geometry. The algebra A_X consists of (0,q)-forms with values in exterior powers of the holomorphic tangent bundle. Its parity is p plus q, the product combines exterior multiplication and polyvector wedge, and the Dolbeault operator is the differential because the tangent bundle powers are holomorphic.

title: Schouten Bracket Before Delta
notes: For any complex manifold, the Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket is already present on polyvector fields and extends to polyvector-valued forms. It has the odd skew symmetry and derivation properties needed for the master equation, but it need not come from a BV operator. The Calabi-Yau condition will supply that missing origin.

title: Maurer-Cartan Versus Master Equation
notes: Connect the appendix directly to Chapter 6. A Beltrami differential phi in A^{0,1}(T_X) satisfies the Maurer-Cartan equation precisely when the corresponding element in the larger algebra satisfies the master equation, up to the harmless normalization used in the appendix. The distinction is conceptual: we deform the differential on the same algebraic model.

title: A Calabi-Yau Volume Form Creates Delta
notes: This is the geometric source of the BV operator. A nowhere-vanishing holomorphic volume form converts polyvectors into ordinary forms by contraction. Transporting the partial operator across that identification gives Delta. Because partial squares to zero and the volume form is holomorphic, Delta squares to zero and anticommutes with the Dolbeault differential.

title: Generalized Tian-Todorov Lemma
notes: Present the lemma as the bridge between the abstract and geometric stories. The Schouten bracket on A_X is generated by Delta in the BV sense, up to the sign convention. Therefore, for a Calabi-Yau manifold, the polyvector-valued Dolbeault algebra is not merely bracketed; it is a full dGBV algebra.

title: Keeping dGBV Under Deformation
notes: The deformation d_phi solves only half the problem: it becomes a differential when the master equation holds. To remain a dGBV algebra with the same Delta, we also need Delta phi equal to zero. In the Calabi-Yau picture, that condition says the contracted form eta(phi) is partial-closed, matching the earlier Tian-Todorov gauge choice.

title: Formal Solutions In A General dGBV Algebra
notes: After the geometric example, the appendix abstracts the Tian-Todorov recursion. The unknown is a formal power series Phi with coefficients in the algebra and polynomial coordinates on cohomology. Phi_1 chooses representatives for cohomology classes, and higher Phi_k terms are correction terms added so the master equation holds order by order.

title: The Two Hypotheses
notes: Make the two extra assumptions feel familiar rather than technical. Finite-dimensional cohomology gives a finite parameter space for formal coordinates. The image identity is the dGBV version of the ddbar lemma: if an element is closed for both d and Delta and is separately d-exact or Delta-exact, it actually comes from dDelta.

title: Recursion: Why Obstructions Disappear
notes: Close with the mechanism, not just the statement. At each degree, previous choices create a quadratic obstruction term. The bracket identity and Delta-closed gauge put that term in the exact rectangle, hypothesis (2) solves it as dDelta of something, and the next correction kills it while staying Delta-closed. This is the abstract Tian-Todorov engine.
